ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows a CMOS inverter: the source terminal of the upper PMOS is connected to 5 V, and the source terminal of the lower NMOS is connected to ground; the gates of the PMOS and NMOS are connected together and driven by 2.5 V; the drains of the two transistors are connected together to form the middle branch, and current I is indicated downward in this branch. From the given conditions, kn = kp = 40 µA/V^2, VTHn = |VTHp| = 1 V. The overdrive voltage of the NMOS is VGS - VTH = 2.5 - 1 = 1.5 V. The overdrive voltage of the PMOS is VSG - |VTHp| = (5 - 2.5) - 1 = 1.5 V. The parameters of the two transistors are symmetric, the current in the series branch is the same, and the symmetric operating point where both transistors are in the saturation region can be taken. Therefore, using the saturation-region current formula I = (1/2)kVOV^2, obtain I = (1/2) × 40 × (1.5)^2 = 45 µA.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: a CMOS inverter has the PMOS at the top tied to 5 V, the NMOS at the bottom tied to ground, both gates driven by 2.5 V, and I marked downward through the common drain branch. From the text take k_n=k_p=40 µA/V^2 and VTHn=|VTHp|=1 V. Compute NMOS overdrive VGS−VTH=2.5−1=1.5 V and PMOS overdrive VSG−|VTHp|=(5−2.5)−1=1.5 V. Because the two series devices must carry the same current and an ideal saturation point is consistent, use the saturation equation for either transistor: I=(1/2)kVOV^2=(1/2)(40)(1.5)^2=45 µA.
